key_insight: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks can be trained with physics-informed residual losses to solve free-boundary PDEs while enforcing obstacle, inequality, complementarity, and boundary constraints.
engineering_relevance: This offers a flexible surrogate solver for contact and interface-dominated PDEs in mechanics, phase change, and related computational engineering problems.
method: KAN approximation of the solution field
Residual-based loss terms for PDE inequalities, obstacle constraints, complementarity, and boundary conditions
Benchmarked against PINN and residual-network baselines
evidence_signal: The abstract reports low relative L2 and L∞ errors and accurate recovery of contact regions and moving interfaces across elliptic, p-Laplacian, and Stefan test problems.
watch_item: Performance is shown on selected benchmark problems, so robustness to more complex geometries, higher dimensions, and training sensitivity still needs validation.
paper_title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Free-Boundary Partial Differential Equations
